title: C-Pin · I-O-I · harmonic boundary reference
purpose: Add a bounded geometric pin controller to the existing Pentagon Crown Return demonstrator and preserve the external spherical-harmonics interface as a comparison source without identifying the mechanisms.

local_control.geometry: one small display pin moves relative to one larger fixed display cylinder and its equatorial boundary
local_control.scope: local deterministic view/control only; no mechanics, collision model, force, material or measured actuator

white_ghost_cross.visual_contract: white perforated and hooked relation lines over the C-Pin boundary view

states.GHOST: projected relation while the pin is strictly inside or outside
states.COINCIDENCE: highlighted relation only at the two declared boundary samples k=25 and k=75

white_ghost_cross.return_requirement: m and n remain separately addressable after the shared view
white_ghost_cross.boundary: The cross visualizes a possible or sampled relation. It is not a material joint, shared state, causal edge or admitted Source Graph relation.

observed_interface: spherical harmonic controls labelled degree l and order m
external_reference.precise_reading: The l=1, m=0 spherical harmonic supplies an axial comparison with an equatorial nodal boundary. It is not evidence that the Crown, C-Pin or Dodeca Heart implements that harmonic mode.

complex_extension_hold.boundary: Mandelbrot, Julia, spherical harmonics, Crown, C-Pin and Dodeca Heart remain distinct objects and views until a typed adapter is declared and tested.

notes: 101 is used here only as the exact discrete sample count and I-O-I display mnemonic.
Prime and exponent associations remain annotations unless a tested mapping supplies inputs, operation and return.

authority.science: Science Desk retains classification and claim-ceiling authority.
authority.source: The external site retains authorship of its interface and visualizations.
